structure: Part 2, Dashboard list, filters, search and sort. Read in full, by line range in backlog.json, the eight dashboard rows inc-017 (lines 677-837, date filter), inc-018 (838-962, three collapsed filter sections), inc-019 (963-1177, three-term search), inc-020 (1178-1382, status filter), inc-021 (2142-2285, list heading "My notifications"), inc-022 (2286-2447, results count copy), inc-024 (2779-2915, sort applies only on submit / "Update sort" button) and inc-023 (2916-3095, sort option labels). Every one has status "blocked". Six (inc-017 to inc-022) carry decision {ruling: "block"} with one identical note: blocked by Rhys on 2026-08-28 because the dashboard is temporary in the animals frontend and moves to trade-imports-ins-frontend; deferred, not rejected, needing a fresh ruling if the dashboard stays. Two (inc-023, inc-024) carry decision {ruling: "defer", ruledAt} by Sam on 2026-08-21: the dashboard is temporary, so no sort work for now. None of the eight has notes, openQuestions or a failure_reason. For each row the claims record the ruling, who made it and when, the reason, any reopening condition, and the difference the ruling parks (from finding.difference), plus the judgements the row itself makes inside finding.difference, finding.correction and provenance.note (band chosen between runs A and C, conditions that must be settled before building, what DR1 leaves unsaid). Provenance notes about run matching, citations, evidence and screens were read for context only.

claims.ref: backlog.json inc-017, decision.ruling and decision.note; status
claims.quote: Blocked by Rhys, 2026-08-28

claims.statement: inc-017 was blocked because the dashboard is temporary in the animals frontend and moves to trade-imports-ins-frontend, so parity work against DR1 dashboard screens buys nothing that travels.

claims.quote: Deferred, not rejected — if the dashboard stays, these need a fresh ruling rather than a re-raise.

claims.statement: The difference blocked by inc-017 is adding a date filter to the dashboard filter panel: three relative-range radios (Today, Tomorrow, Next seven days) and a start and end date pair using the MoJ date picker DR1 uses.
claims.quote: Add a date filter to the dashboard's filter panel: the three relative-range radios and a start/end date pair using the MoJ date picker DR1 uses.

claims.statement: DR1 never states which date the dashboard date filter applies to; the row reads it as the arrival date at destination but says the prototype never demonstrates it and the design never says it.
claims.quote: Which date it filters on has to be stated, and the design does not state it anywhere — the section is headed "By date", its visually hidden legend reads "Choose a date range" and the two fields are only "Start date" and "End date". ... So arrival at destination is the reading, but the prototype never demonstrates it and the design never says it.
claims.note: Recorded as a gap because the row itself says the design is silent on the filtered date; the arrival-date reading is the row's inference, not a ruling.

claims.statement: inc-017 judges that the date filter needs the notifications endpoint to accept a date range before the control can do anything, and that the relative radios should be built on that same range parameter rather than as three more parameters.
claims.quote: the notifications endpoint has to accept a date range before the control can do anything. Build the relative radios on top of the same range parameter rather than as three more parameters.

claims.statement: inc-017 records that DR1's date filter is inert: the sidebar is in no form, and a chosen date is not even echoed back after a page load.
claims.quote: Like the rest of the sidebar it is markup only — the sidebar is in no form, and getDashboardViewModel reads dateRange, startDate and endDate but never filters the list by any of them
claims.note: finding.correction adds: "so a chosen date is not even echoed back after a page load."

claims.statement: inc-024 sets the rule for settling it: if the missing button is a design decision, the frontend submits the sort form when the select changes and drops "Update sort", keeping the button visible as a no-JavaScript fallback; if it is prototype incompleteness, the frontend is already right and the finding is struck.
claims.quote: Settle it before doing anything: if it is a design decision, the frontend should submit the form when the select changes and drop the "Update sort" button from src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:63-82, with a no-JavaScript fallback that keeps the button visible. If it is prototype incompleteness, the frontend is already right and this finding is struck.

claims.statement: inc-024 records that DR1 gives no evidence its sort select works at all: the route reads the sort value but never orders the list, the select's GET form has no submit button, and no script submits it on change.
claims.ref: backlog.json inc-024, finding.difference, finding.correction and finding.verification
claims.quote: Design release 1 gives no evidence its select works at all: it is inert in three separate ways.

claims.statement: inc-024 records that the frontend's filter panel follows the same pattern as sort: its "Search" button is the only way to apply the keyword, while DR1's filter panel has no button.
claims.quote: The same pattern applies to the filter panel, whose "Search" button is the only way to apply the keyword.

claims.statement: The backlog holds that a person's ruling on a finding stands even when the other discovery run raised the same finding and left it open: run C's deferral of the sort findings stands over run A's open finding.
claims.quote: Run C's deferral stands even though run A found the same thing and left it open: a finding a person has already ruled on does not come back to life because the other run also raised it.
